title: Storybook: 44 Track Fairy Tale Music Pack
tagline: 44 fairy tale music tracks for any game engine. A music box opens every full piece.
description:
Storybook is a 44 track fairy tale music pack for any game engine: one book in five chapters, and a music box storyteller opens every full piece.

It ships 38 full looping pieces and 6 short cues as OGG and editable MIDI, royalty free for commercial games, with three full tracks free on this page.

What is inside

44 tracks · 38 loops · 6 cues · OGG + editable MIDI · 54:53

  • Five chapters of one tale: Once Upon a Time (9), Into the Wood (9), The Spell (6), The Trial (8) and Happily Ever After (6), plus 6 cues: Once, A Wish, The Spell Is Cast, Treasure, And So They Won and The Book Closes.
  • The storyteller: a music box opens all 38 full pieces alone, playing the album's first theme before the scene begins, and is heard nowhere else. It is its own part in the MIDI, and every loop point sits after it, so in a game the opening plays once.
  • The spell: in the 15 tracks under it (Chapters 3 and 4 and one cue) the first theme is played only upside down, never in its own shape. It comes back the right way up in The Spell Breaks.
  • A small band: woodwinds, strings, harp, keys, bells, voices and one timpani. No brass and no drum kit on any track.
  • One seed theme, Once Upon a Time, beside seven more for the child, home, the wood, the spell, the fairy, the beast and the ending.
  • Every full piece loops (the shortest loop is 45.0 seconds), with LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags in its OGG file.
  • 29 General MIDI instruments, among them music box, celesta, harp, harpsichord, oboe, ocarina, recorder and choir aahs.

The theory and audio reports (788 and 510 checks, 0 failed) ship inside the download.

The book: every track in its chapter, the storyteller's notes, and the first theme drawn the way each shipped MIDI states it, upright or upside down.

Before, under and after the spell: the storyteller's opening drawn note for note from three of the shipped files.

The score sheet: all 44 tracks, from Once Upon a Time to The Book Closes.

Works with

RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop tags with no plugin. The Readme gives import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Any engine that plays OGG can use the files, and the MIDI lets you score it with your own sounds or drop the storyteller.

Try it free

Three full tracks with their MIDI are free on this page: Hearthside (a home scene, the storyteller first), The Witch Queen (the final boss, under the spell) and The Spell Breaks (the theme the right way up again). More free tracks from our other albums: Overture, the free sampler.

Licence and how it was made

Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. Do not resell the tracks as music assets. Every track is composed in code and rendered through a General MIDI soundfont; no generative audio model was used. The code and the cover art were made with AI tools. Every tune was composed for this record; no game or film cue is quoted and no traditional tune is used.

Versions

v1.0 (1 November 2026): first release, 44 tracks.

devlog.title: Storybook is out: a 44 track fairy tale score read aloud by a music box
devlog.body:
Storybook is a 44 track music pack for fairy tale games: one book in five chapters, from the village and the cottage through the wicked wood, a curse and a trial to a happy ending, plus 6 short cues. It is live now, $9.99, with three full tracks free on the page.

The idea. A music box is the storyteller. It opens every one of the 38 full pieces alone, with the album's first theme, and plays nowhere else. Then a spell falls: in the 15 tracks under it that theme is only ever heard upside down, until The Spell Breaks. The band is small on purpose: woodwinds, strings, harp, keys, voices and one timpani, with no brass and no drums.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. Where the music box sounds, which way up the theme is on each track and the loop tags were each measured on the shipped files, and the loop tags were followed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project. Every loop point sits after the storyteller, so in a game the opening plays once.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; the MIDI is there so you can move it to your own sounds, or drop the storyteller. No game or film cue is quoted and no traditional tune is used. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model was used; the cover art was made with AI tools.

https://csaf.itch.io/storybook
